title: MV Hero's without Borders (héroes sin fronteras)

posts.author: Cenewulf_TTV
posts.body:
​
SECTION A: SYNOPSIS
Spoiler
In Heroes Without Borders, you play as Sigvar and his friends as they navigate the world as the newest recruits of the Adventurers' guild.  The overall gameplay loop plays out like your old school 90's RPG with a couple of those little things from that day. The intentions for the writing for this game are a fun "You spoony bard" coded script in the beginning that slowly hits Metal Gear's thematics about war, war economies, deterrence, and information control. The goal is to make an RPG that respects your time as the player while also giving you a ton of replay value. It took an immense amount of time, but once I got Aerosys' random dungeon plugin configured the way I needed it, I was able to create a full-on ATB-based mystery dungeon experience. While the Demo only contains the first mystery dungeon, the goal is for there to eventually be a random chance that an area turns into a mystery dungeon instead of its normal path. The way I set up the skill learn system is that it operates more or less like the magic shops in the first Final Fantasy, but each character has their own pseudo skill tree, save for a couple of overlaps coming later in development. I still need to set up the separate notetags, but the day and night system has been added tentatively, and I am making tweaks to events.
Summary of the main features of the demo:
1-2 Hours of story-based content, 4 hours of content if you want to learn all of the skills and see everything, according to initial feedback.
ATB Battlesystem (Yanfly)
Animations for some attacks utilizing the action sequence pack by Yanfly (more will get fleshed out with time)
Skill learn system via Yanfly.
Custom music composed by me and other artists is credited in the end credits.
A mystery dungeon concept via a combination of Aerosys' random dungeon plugin, with battleprocessing events (Monster sprites moving on the map with YEP event chase) and loot common events mimicking the usual results of opening a chest in a mystery dungeon: loot, a buff/debuff/heal, or a monster in a box.
Day and Night system in early phases courtesy of Moghunter
The way the Battle system works is sort of like the concept of optimal combos in fighting games, only without doing the inputs since I don't have that awesome plugin by Vizustella(I think?) Melee characters, like Sigvar and Astrid, will have some form of an AOE opener, her's being either an AOE attack or her taunt, and then using the TP gained from that and or the amount gained from being the main target, you can then start using your Meter (TP) to do your special attacks. Each character has a "Focus" Skill that allows you to use 50 TP to restore 30% of your MP. Using 2 of them would be like taking a short rest in D&D. That comes in the clutch for magic characters because they are a simpler route of just using TP to recharge MP without needing to use Ethers, etc.
I am still working on the gold and general economy, but the idea is that it operates like FFXII in that the fangs, pelts, and even weaker equipment being sold are how you make your money in addition to chests. I felt like this could ease up on the grind a bit when it comes to upgrading. For current demo purposes, you'll really only need to equip whatever new weapons you find. I intend to change it so that the characters will only start with the Weapon, Head slot, and Body slot. This will be gradual, as I am sure this will increase the time it takes to test changes, since there would be a necessary grind for armor, etc. Willing to adjust the armor at the first major shop to coincide with the next logical upgrade if feedback recommends it.
Updates coming with V0.2 (tba), more mystery dungeons added to the main story, and the demo extended up to the next 2 back-to-back mystery dungeons. Initial phase testing of YEP's item durability (can't have a good mystery dungeon without something being able to break!)
IMAGES/SCREENSHOTS
Spoiler
SECTION B: CHARACTERS
Spoiler
Sigvar
In silent whispers from woods afar,
A familiar howl carried by northern winds.
A blade once tempered by loss and honor,
Now marches forth toward destiny's flame.
Not much is known about Sigvar’s lineage. He was raised by the Exiled Swordsmaster Halvar as a child. After a little over 20 years under his tutelage, Sigvar sets out with his new friends Astrid, Alva, and Fennwick. It was only within the past year that he met them in Porthos when he was getting supplies to bring back to his home. Having a whole village step up to raise them, the three empathized with Sigvar and took him in when Halvar passed. After that year and integrating himself into society, Sigvar felt the call of adventure and that the winds of adventure were blowing his way.
Astrid
A stern face before joyous laughter
She did not ask to grow up fast.
Fate demanded it.
With Axe in hand, she perseveres.
Proud daughter of Porthos, Astrid fights with resolute force and knightly honor. Trained in spear and axe, she commands the field with both discipline and destruction. She defends allies while crushing foes with sweeping arcs and piercing charges. Her scar was part of an unfortunate accident with Thornlashes when she was a child.
Fennwick
Gifted in magic and archery
He was never one to leave the village.
But adventure calls even the most unsuspecting.
Growing up with his big sister Astrid, meant always being in arm's reach for Fennwick. One day, when they were children, he wandered too far and got lost in Fenrir Meadows. Astrid found him surrounded by Thornlashes and, after grabbing a sturdy enough branch, began swinging it wildly. She managed to chase them off, but not without a few scares. Out of concern for his sister, Fennwick felt something flow through him as he placed his hand on her now bloody face, and she was healed all except for. As a personal promise to himself, he took up archery so that he could take out trouble beforehand. The alternative was his sister constantly worrying about him and intervening.
Alva
Magic called to her like a sweet song.
And the spells she weaves are like a siren’s
Deadly and alluring
If only she could remember the spells to begin with
Daughter to one of the Eldari Conclave’s court mages, she was cast out at an early age. The conclave is regularly frowned upon by the other factions due to their views on children who don’t grow up in their view as normal. It wasn’t that our favorite mage wasn’t smart. She’s BRILLIANT. However, after a few mishaps in early classes, as well as one incident that almost caused the floating city of Ygvalin to start plummeting towards the sea. It was her fault, sure. She was a bit more overeager, but what child isn’t? “Demon,” “defective child!” and all other nasty things were said to her before she was carted off to Porthos. The same day, the Witch of the Woods, Brynhilda, was just leaving town and saw the child crying as a cart rode off in the distance. “What’s your problem, Missy?” It didn’t take long after she saw the Conclave’s seal that she knew what was going on. “Listen here, kiddo. How about you come have a nice meal with me, and we can start figuring out life tomorrow. Now grab your stuff and stop crying. Those court jesters don’t see it, but I see something special in your girl.” It was the first time someone believed in her. A stranger no less. In the years to come, she faced many challenges. She would have months of spells going off without a hitch, and then a random day, she couldn’t remember even the most basic of cantrips. Now her time has come to join the guild.
SECTION C: STORYLINE/PLOT
Spoiler
In ages long past. There was a conflict between all the races of the planet Orokin IV. The magical arms race between the Humans, Dwarves, Elves, FaeFolk, and various other Beastkin tribes led to a fracturing event. The once massive landmass began to fracture as portals began to form across the planet. Some of the more magically astute societies were already living in their terraformed islands in the sky, but still faced merciless hordes in the skies. The king Æthelwulf Stormchaser had found himself at a crossroads. [This portion has been redacted as per Guild Charter 56.152c]. Rather than choose to continue bloodshed in a war on multiple fronts, he rallied the free peoples of Orokin IV together against the hordes from the veil. After a grueling united front for roughly three years, the portals began to close, save one. It is atop Mt. Kordella that a portal still stirs. A constant reminder of the consequences of unchecked ambition. A thousand years passed, and while we do not know what caused the fracturing and the hordes to invade, Æthelwulf knew that if war continued, the hordes would come back. In an effort to keep the peace, Æthelwulf renounced his title as King and instead made a decree:
“Whoever is loyal to protecting our realm from the hordes beyond the veil, follow me. Shed yourselves from the skin of nationality and stand with me against the real enemy of our world.”
Æthelwulf then formed the first Adventurer’s guild on the outskirts west of Mt. Kordella. For the next thousand or so years, the guild stood as a line of defense in case the monsters ever returned. Various moments would demonstrate their necessity as Kordella and other areas became hotbeds for them to slowly trickle out. A thousand years later, we come to our newest recruits, Sigvar, Astrid, Fennwick, and Alva.
DOWNLOAD LINK
Spoiler

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Heyas, I gave your demo a try and it worked this time! I played through the tournament and decided to call it quits due to a mix of things. There's a lot of great world building here, but I think before speeding ahead with content it would be worthwhile to polish what you currently have.
Spoiler:
Feedback
As I said the world building is neat and I liked the personalities I saw in each character, even if I didn't get to spend a lot of time with them. I do feel like the intro dragged on a bit too long since I don't think it was necessary to scroll over the world map or have scrolling text describe so much about the current times and the upcoming tournament. A lot of that could be shared naturally between the party on their way to the city.
There were a few spots where I think you forgot that the player won't be as familiar with the game as you are. The menu includes a quest journal, but I didn't receive a single quest the entire time I was playing! For the most part I knew what I should be doing, but having simple "go here" quest updates would have made things a lot more clear. I also spent way too long trying to figure out where the explosion happened in the first town because the wording wasn't clear enough. The party mentioned an explosion at the entrance of the town, so I ran there and found nothing. So then I went to the world map, assuming someone was attacking, and found nothing. Then I wandered the town aimlessly until I tried the damaged house's door... Which hadn't be unlocked before! Having flames and smoke coming off the roof would have made it obvious where the explosion came from. Gently nudging your players into the right direction with quest notices and events on maps can keep your players engaged and make sure that nobody ends up lost and confused about what to do next.
Combat seems like an important part of the game, so I have to admit that I'm confused why you chose to use an ATB system at the moment. None of the starting skills seemed to be faster than any other, which made the timers feel like they were just there to slow down the battles. To me it felt like a normal turn-based system would work just as well or even better than the ATB since I wouldn't have to wait as long for each party member to attack. Perhaps time and speed comes into play later in the game, but since the intro is your one chance to hook your players on your combat you should make sure that it's showing off its good points. If Sigvar had two attack skills, one that hits once but hits quickly and one that hits harder but is much slower, you would be teaching your players to think about what skill to use depending on their situation right from the start. Everyone's skills seemed to fit them well, but the system itself just didn't feel like it was being showcased and ended up making battles a bit boring.
I was going to just touch on the mapping, but things kinda spiraled out of control.
I ended up recreating two of the maps, so if you'd like an in-depth explanation of the changes I made and why read the spoiler below. If you want the TLDR, it would be to drastically decrease the size of your maps and map with purpose and confidence.
Spoiler:
A mapping tangent
Let's start by pointing out something wrong with Sigvar's house: it's way too big! Sigvar could host an entire troop of guards in the house and still have empty space left over. Beyond that, I'm left wondering how Sigvar and his master could live there together when there's only one bedroom. Sure, Sigvar could sleep in the empty living room, but there's no hint of bedding or storage there. There is also an issue with mismatched wall heights, the back wall is two tiles tall while the walls around the bedroom are only one tile tall.
Here's my take on the house. I cut the size down drastically so that the kitchen and living room area is condensed, and adjusted all the walls so that they are consistently two tiles tall. I lined the kitchen wall with the counters and cut the number of shelves down to one in there since they wouldn't have needed quite so many bottles of wine and supplies (though with some tileset editing you could make it look even better). I also added in a second smaller bedroom where Sigvar would have slept before his master passed, and then used tiles to do some environmental storytelling: Sigvar has had trouble cooking before so the ground in front of the oven is dirty and he has turned his old bedroom into a storage room where some supplies and his master's old stool now rests. My remake has all the important details that yours included, but the smaller size and more condensed tile use makes it feel cozier and more lived-in.
The next map is the hedge maze in Fenrir Meadow. I was pretty surprised to enter the forest on the world map and then be confronted by a hedge maze, but I think the area's biggest issue is the lack of visual interest. The hedges are all tall and the paths are small so it feels very claustrophobic, and the square hedges makes it feel like the location was man-made when I think it's supposed to be a wild area.
My remake ditches the hedges entirely and relies on trees to keep the party on the path. I'll admit that I had thought the area was meant to be a forest when I was mapping instead of a Meadow, but I think the general concepts would still work if you used hills and dense grasses instead of trees. I kept the exact same paths as the original just to show how different it can look, but I would say that cutting down on the dead ends or merging them into open areas would probably look better. Instead of using the hedges to keep the player on the path I used clusters of trees with some spaces between them to force the player to walk where I want while still having some empty spaces to look at. I only used two trees for this, but adding in flowers, bushes, and rocks would make it even more interesting to look at.
There are so many mapping tutorials to learn from (
Avery
alone
has made
so many
tutorials
that can take
your mapping skills
to the
next
level
) and you can always look at other devs' maps in the
screenshot thread
to see how they create lovely maps. Mapping in rpg maker is something that any dev can do well with practice, so go give all your maps some more love and attention!
There were a few other bugs and oddities:
The game's name on the title screen is wrong, it says "Hero's without Borders" when it should be "Heroes Without Borders"
The game froze during the intro scene while the world map was scrolling. I don't know how or why it happened, but the FPS dropped to 0 and the whole game froze. Restarted and it didn't happen again
Sigvar's outfit drastically changes color during the intro
All of the enemies are set as if it was a frontview battle, so they're all too close to the party
Astrid can use Cleave in the menu, wasting TP
Can walk through the gravestones in the city cemetery
Can walk though the pillars in the city weapon/armor shop
And lastly, a few minor gripes I had while playing. These are all subjective so whether or not you want to make any of these changes is all up to you and what you want out of your project.
Spoiler
Why mix message boxes with scrolling text in the intro? Sticking with one or the other would be more consistent
While I often say that tints are important, they shouldn't be eye-searing. Tone down the bright red one, unless the world is on fire
If you aren't going to have lots of interactable tiles, make sure places that have items are obvious. I only checked the cupboard because of the comment by Sigvar, but if I only searched a few of the shelves I wouldn't have found the items and would think there are no hidden items in the game
World maps should decrease the amount of walking the player has to do, not be giant open spaces. At least in the start have Sigvar be near the first town, so that the player can easily tell where to go (and so they avoid fighting too many enemies alone)
Overall, you've clearly put a lot of heart into this game. The story is intriguing, but unfortunately the gameplay and presentation is letting it down. Luckily that can be fixed with more time and polish, so I'm sure you can make this game into something that players eagerly await being finished.
Good luck with your project!

I appreciate the feedback. This is my first project and ive been doing it solo outside of help from a handful of people who tuned into the twitch stream. Definitely drastically different than what a few content creators told me. The intro drags because I tried to make it roughly as long as the intro track that plays. I guess i should probably start making more condensed versions of my songs for the games purposes. Its a little hard when youre an improv/jam musician but I can figure that out. I wish I had had this kind of feedback a few months ago when I was still unemployed and had a lot more time on my hands (started a new FT gig last Friday and I start fall semester monday ) to make these changes. End of the day I dont want to put slop out there since it is also an in memory of project to my grandma so ill definitely start working on polishing things. Right now ive got a couple artists that I met at a game jam helping me with a new tileset as well as Sigvar &co that matches the SNES Era vibe of the marumagi sprites that come post tournament (which im sure the clash of art style between it and the vanilla assets would have been another point of contention/critique). The quest system im still trying to figure out exactly to point peeps in the right direction.
Also one last note:
Thank you for agreeing me on the grammar for the title. I went with Heroes first and then changed it because I had a bunch of people go "Dude its Hero's" and then started second guessing my own English LOL

4 months later almost and I finally have time to actually pop over here LOL. The new job is kick ass. Like there was a literal biscuits and gravy day and I'm getting lot's of good feedback from my manager. Especially since I pushed for it and got this place after 12 years of going without one
to have an actual system image in place instead of having to manually install literally everything on every machine LOL.
I took a lot of your feedback to heart and also a good bit of feedback I've gotten from the showcase I got to present it at a couple weeks ago. A few folks from either here or reddit have been popping into the twitch streams of the development as well lately and giving me tips and pointers to help me along when I couldn't google the answer or find a tutorial lol
The intro is now just the long scrolling text about the year with some minor thematic changes just from how much narrative has evolved as I got settled into the job.
I got a handle on the speed settings finally so now the pacing should feel like that FFV-FFVI speed with basic attacks and some specials being instant and some taking time to charge. There's also a lite tutorial for each of the first 4 characters that pops in with a short blurb about their general roles in combat. I didn't want it to be super overbearing and say what each starting skill does down to the letter. Since I'm using Yanfly's skill learn system, I'm now working on passive increase style skills as well as more ways to spend JP earned.
It's still tentative but HP and damage Scaling should be better as well to make the early fights go quicker and there was a bit of a revamp to the first area. Maybe it's just cause I like open areas but I made the Fenrir meadows a larger forest (No more Hedge maze xD) I remember you saying map with intent so I added treasures and planned encounters throughout the map as well as an introduction to the crystal system in place that showed up after the tournament in the version you played.
As far as direction, World map encounters are off. I am looking into ways I can make other types of encounters on the map. Like a traveling merchant or maybe dialogue options that can lead to a fight or loot. It's also much clearer which way to go now from sigvars house and with the world map encounters off, you're free to basically go wherever you have access to. I kept the distance intact due to thematic reasons. An Exile wouldn't probably live right near a town. Alva's house has little flames that show up on the roof and a nice little dialog change of Sigvar saying that sounded like it happened near the Inn instead of the entrance to down. I'm also doing daily pass throughs and trying to add more interactables to spots I missed.
The story beats are still the same but I think you might see a noticeable difference in the way the game plays out now compared to the first time. I had a sprite artist and a concept artist as well as someone helping with my idea of a 16 bit version of the rtp assets but the sprite and concept artist had to take a step back but the main cast now have their own sprites instead of the rtp assets and Alva currently has a battler sprite as well. I'll probably make a post in the other appropriate threads to see if other folks wanna help me see this vision come to life. Would love to get your feedback on how it is now compared to a few months ago
Edit to add also happy new year
